title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.



I’m a student in the MUSA program at Penn. My background is in international affairs and geography, and I’m interested in remote sensing, water resources, immigrant identities, and generally using GIS for good.




Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course
About — more background and how to reach me

title: About Me
text:
Before joining the MUSA program, I graduated from The George Washington University in Washington D.C. I received a Bachelor of Science in International Affairs and Geography with a minor in Geographic Information Systems. During my undergraduate degree I studied at Queen’s University Belfast and Université Paris Dauphine. In Belfast, I developed original research on immigrant integration in post-conflict cities funded by the GW Undergraduate Research Award. In Paris, I expanded my knowledge of immigrant communities in the EU and became proficient in French. Before my bachelors, I received an International Baccalaureate Diploma at the United World College in Maastricht, The Netherlands.
I am passionate about urban spatial analysis because I believe access to data and productively educating the public with data visualizations is a core pillar of our world. I love cities and learning about the different layers that form a city’s unique identity. I hope to gain skills in programming and research methods that can aid in my future workplace or in pursuit of a PhD.

title: Week 1
text:
What is a Website? a folder of html files + a computer that is always on we are going to be using Quarto + GitHub What is Quarto? makes .qmd files that you write → magic quarto machine → html files magic is made by clicking render what happens in the machine — reads the file from top to bottom finds the code chunks sends them to R, gets results glues the text + the results into html if there is an error the magic does not happen Anatomy of a .qmd
Files + Folders Who is this file for? For me files vs For the machine For me For machine index.qmd _quarto.yml (settings for the whole website) about.qmd _freeze/ (for quarto after it gets rendered Do not touch) weekly_notes/.qmd .Rproj → Rstudio assignments/.qmd .gitignore → Github
.renviron → R (secrets)
docs/ → the internet i.e. where your website lives
“Index” website rule: ask for a folder, you get that folder index.html carennakt.github.io/ → docs/index.html /weekly-notes → docs/weekly.notes/index.html GIT/GitHub.com/GitHub desktop GIT is a version tracker, invisible, runs on your computer commit → “save a labeled snapshot” (lives on your computer) push → “send my snapshot to GitHub.com” GitHub.com is a website that stores a copy of your folder GitHub desktop are buttons that tell GIT what to do .Rscript code only sandbox good for working out the problems, experimenting, sketch book, In console you can run stuff real quick but it doesnt save repository is like a larger folder that you wanna share w the world on githun Workflow everyweek you will download a .qmd file and put it into assignments along w some data make sure to have highlighted your index.qmd when you are rendering you want to click on index when you press render commit is different from saving – commit saves since the last time you committed then you push it to github.com C:-portfolio
